Updated take integrating Beige Book insights:
- The FOMC’s June 2019 statement is modestly positive on growth and the labor market, with below-target inflation and rising uncertainties; policy was held steady, with one dissent in favor of a cut.
- Beige Book-style evidence for the April to mid-May period points to slight-to-moderate growth across Districts, strong labor markets with notable shortages (especially low-skill), and modest wage pressures. Consumer spending was steady and tourism stronger in the Southeast, while manufacturing and residential construction contributed but were not broad-based surges.
- Credit signals are cooler: banks tightened standards for C&I and construction/land development loans and other terms across firm sizes; demand softened for construction/land development, HELOCs, credit cards, and other consumer loans (auto and subprime mortgage demand largely unchanged). This aligns with “soft” business fixed investment and below-target inflation in the FOMC statement and raises downside risk to capex and CRE as risk appetite cools.

Net effect: still modestly positive, but more cautious than a macro-only read. Adjusting the tone slightly downward from earlier, to reflect tighter credit supply and softer loan demand.
